summary: Milestone 2026.05.266 produced zero experiments in the timing window — the same structural pattern that has recurred across many consecutive milestones. The timing-script look-back epoch is not anchored to the conductor-state.json activation timestamp, so all real milestone work falls outside the measured window. The milestone was additionally impacted by an ongoing pre-test cascade failure that blocked the conductor from dispatching non-retro research tasks.
bottlenecks_identified: Timing-script look-back window is not anchored to conductor-state.json activated_at timestamp — root cause of all consecutive empty-timing-window retros; wall-clock work is happening but is invisible to this metric layer.

Pre-test cascade blocking the conductor has persisted across multiple milestones; the task designated to repair it was itself subject to the same gate that was failing, creating a structural deadlock that requires outer-loop (operator or Claude outer-loop) intervention rather than an in-conductor fix.
No post-activation dispatch verification gate exists; the conductor can complete a full milestone with zero non-retro experiments dispatched and the retro is the only artifact that surfaces this.
No same-session first-dispatch discipline is mechanically enforced; the first non-retro experiment is not guaranteed to launch within the same conductor session as milestone activation.
improvements_suggested: Fix timing-script look-back to use conductor-state.json activated_at as the epoch boundary instead of a rolling wall-clock window; this will make timing data meaningful for every future milestone.

Wire a zero-artifact alarm that fires at 60 minutes post-activation if no non-retro experiment artifact has been committed; surfaces the empty-dispatch pattern within the same session rather than only at retro time.
Enforce same-session first-dispatch discipline mechanically in the conductor: the activation step should queue and launch at least one non-retro experiment before writing the activation artifact.

Address the pre-test cascade failure at the outer-loop level (operator or outer-loop Claude session), not as a conductor-gated task; the structural deadlock requires a layer above the conductor to break the cycle.

Add a pre-launch check that verifies the test suite is passing before milestone activation, and blocks activation if the pre-test gate is already failing — preventing the cascade from propagating into the next milestone.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix the timing-script look-back epoch to conductor-state.json activated_at — this single change unblocks 40+ milestones of invisible operational data and restores the retro's ability to identify real bottlenecks.
Break the pre-test cascade deadlock at the outer-loop scope (operator session) rather than queuing another in-conductor fix task; a failing test gate cannot self-heal from inside the conductor.
Wire a 60-minute post-activation zero-artifact alarm so the empty-dispatch pattern is surfaced and actionable within the same conductor session instead of only at retro close.
meta_reflection: This retro is the latest in a long series of structurally identical retros: empty timing window, zero experiments in scope, the same root-cause diagnosis repeated. The operational discipline of writing accurate retros is functioning correctly — the retro faithfully reports what it can measure. What is not functioning is the feedback loop: the root cause (timing-epoch misconfiguration + pre-test cascade) has been diagnosed accurately for many consecutive milestones but has not been repaired because the repair requires action at a layer above the conductor. The highest-leverage meta-improvement is not another task in the conductor but a direct outer-loop intervention to fix the timing script and unblock the test suite.
